title: All the Events, Matchers, Handler Types

questions.prompt: Your hook must fire for the project's own Edit tool but never for NotebookEdit, and it must fire for every tool from an MCP server named `memory`. Which matcher set does that?
questions.explanation: The moment a matcher contains characters outside letters, digits, _, -, spaces, commas and |, the whole string becomes an unanchored JavaScript regex — so `^Edit$` anchors it to exactly Edit (which is what excludes NotebookEdit), and `mcp__memory__.*` matches the server's tools. Option B fails on the MCP side: bare `mcp__memory__` has no dot or anchor, so it would also match a server named `memory_dump`. Option C's `Edit.*` is unanchored and matches NotebookEdit, which is the exact exclusion you asked for. Option D gets the anchors but uses `^` on the MCP side with no trailing wildcard, so it can't match any tool name.

questions.prompt: Two PreToolUse handlers disagree: one returns permissionDecision 'allow' and another returns 'deny'. What does the harness do?
options: Deny wins — precedence is deny > defer > ask > allow
The last handler in the file wins
The most recently edited settings file wins
The user is prompted to break the tie
questions.explanation: Hooks don't vote and don't last-write-wins; the precedence ladder is deny > defer > ask > allow, so one deny ends it regardless of what anything else said. Options B and C invent ordering rules that don't exist — settings levels merge rather than shadow, and within a level there's no documented last-wins behaviour. Option D is the intuitive guess and the wrong one: a hook decision is made outside the permission prompt, so the user never sees this tie to break.

questions.prompt: Your PostToolUse hook exits 2 with a clear stderr reason after the agent edits a file you don't want edited. The file still exists. The agent mentions your reason on its next turn. Is the hook broken?
options: No — PostToolUse can't block; exit 2 there sends stderr into the model's context, which is what happened
Yes — you must have attached it to the wrong matcher, since the handler ran
Yes — exit 2 only blocks when the event carries a matcher
No — but only because hook failures default to continuing
questions.explanation: That's PostToolUse behaving correctly: it fires after the tool ran, so the edit is irreversible from the hook's position, and exit 2's role there is to hand the reason to the model as a system reminder. If you wanted the write refused, the event is PreToolUse. Option B is wrong because the handler demonstrably ran. Option C confuses matcher support with blocking capability — they're independent columns in the event table. Option D misattributes the outcome to failure handling: nothing failed here, and the stderr was delivered deliberately, not as a notice.

questions.prompt: A handler declared on SessionStart with `"if": "Bash(git *)"` never runs, and produces no error. Why?
options: `if` is only evaluated on PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest and PermissionDenied — elsewhere a handler with `if` never runs, silently
`if` cannot be combined with a matcher on the same group
`if` requires a newer Claude Code than the rest of the config
`if` only works on `command` handlers, and yours is a `prompt` handler
questions.explanation: The silent case is the documented behaviour: `if` is evaluated on five tool events and nowhere else, so a handler carrying one is simply skipped on SessionStart with no diagnostic. That's worth knowing precisely because nothing tells you. Option B invents an incompatibility that doesn't exist — `if` and matcher coexist on tool events. Option C is half-true about version gates but the wrong field; `if` itself is long-standing. Option D misreads the constraint: `if` is event-limited, not handler-type-limited.
